Which countries in Europe are moving forward in the field of electronic voting?
In Europe, Belgium is one of our largest and most important customers. Actually, the last elections we ran and supported were the European Parliament elections in May, for Belgium. At the same time, we ran a pilot in Bulgaria that is looking into bringing in technology and innovation in elections and we’re looking into bringing in technology and integrity into the election process.
Key words for us are bringing efficiency and transparency to government. In the election market, why would countries bring in technological advancement in elections often still done on paper? Because it increases integrity, it increases security.
But in addition to that, it makes voting more accessible. More people can vote, in an easier way, in a more convenient way. And it brings the cost of running elections down and the speed of running them up. And lastly, it is a lot greener as most paper-based elections.
In Estonia, over 30% of voters cast their ballot via the internet in the European elections in May.
Right now, the internet voting system in Estonia already has about ten years of experience. So they have been investing in research and experimenting and growing their internet voting system for the past ten years.
Do you see this system of online voting, from home, expanding to other countries soon?
Internet voting is something that we are now beginning to offer to our customers. We made an investment into internet voting for Estonia. Estonia is the most successful internet voting experience we’ve seen in the world. We can take this experience and make this available to the rest of the world.
Now, internet voting has certain challenges in itself, which are completely different from traditional voting. The most persistent one has to do with online identity. How can you verify that someone online is really the person he is said to be? It’s not only a problem for internet voting, but also for bank transactions or booking services; it is a general challenge.
We’re also not betting or claiming that everyone will start voting online to elect their government, by next week. That’s not what we’re after. We want to offer an additional channel of voting, next to going to a polling station.

User: Elaborate on the impact of modern digital technology on art, discussing advancements in style, content, and accessibility.
Assistant: Modern digital technology has had a significant impact on art, and we can see its influence in various spheres. The advancements in technology have led to a shift in the creative approach of artists, and new ways of creating and distributing art have emerged.

One of the most significant advancements in style has been the use of digital tools to create artworks. Advancements in software and hardware have made it possible for artists to create works that are more intricate, vibrant, and dynamic than ever before. Digital tools like graphics tablets, 3D printers, and digital paintbrushes and canvases have enabled artists to produce art in ways that were previously impossible.

Moreover, digital art has allowed for the exploration of previously unexplored themes and styles. With the development of new visual effects, art that explores abstract concepts such as the intersection of literature, sound, and visual art has gained more popularity.

The content and medium of digital art have also experienced a revolution. Artists have been able to create digital installations, interactive artworks, and virtual reality experiences. These new forms of art allow audiences to be more fully involved in the artistic process and experience art like never before.

Accessibility has also undergone transformation. Through digital media, artists can now reach a global audience without having to leave their studio. Social media platforms like Instagram have made it easier for artists to promote their work, connect with other artists, and collaborate on projects. The internet has also made it possible for enthusiasts and collectors to view and purchase artwork from all over the world, promoting art as a commodity.

In conclusion, modern digital technology has enabled artists and enthusiasts alike to embrace and explore art in ways that were impossible just a few years ago. As technology continues to evolve, no doubt, we can expect even more significant advances in style, content, and accessibility.
User: Thanks for elaborating on the impact of modern digital technology on art. Can you provide more information on how digital technology has influenced the way art is received and interpreted by society? I'm particularly interested in how digital art has challenged traditional notions of art and beauty.
Assistant: Sure, I would be happy to share more on this topic.

The emergence of digital art has disrupted traditional notions of art and beauty in several ways. Firstly, digital art is often created using tools and techniques that challenge traditional artistic practices. Digital art often includes elements like coding, programming, and interactive elements, which were not present in traditional art forms.

The incorporation of these elements has expanded the definition of what can be considered art. Some might argue that digital art has challenged traditional forms of art by questioning the idea of what art can be, and what it means to produce art in modern times.

Moreover, digital art has challenged traditional notions of beauty by presenting new forms of aesthetics. Digital tools offer possibilities to create art that is less representational and more abstract, allowing for an exploration of new ideas and aesthetics.

One example of this is glitch art. Glitch art involves manipulating digital data to create random, often abstract or distorted images that challenge traditional notions of beauty, symmetry, and form. Another example is generative art, which reflects a desire to create art that simulates natural processes, resulting in strikingly complex and beautiful images.

Digital platforms have also enabled contemporary artists to integrate their artwork with digital media, effectively incorporating technology as a part of their creative process. Additionally, digital art has resulted in new forms of artistic collaboration, facilitating the creation and distribution of new types of art and ideas.

As a result of these developments, the way art is received and interpreted by society has changed. Digital art is often presented in non-traditional spaces like galleries, museums, and online platforms. This allows a broader audience to experience and engage with artistic ideas from different cultures and perspectives.

In conclusion, digital technology has had a profound impact on the way we produce and consume art, challenging traditional notions of what it means to be an artist, what art can be, and what beauty represents. As we continue to advance technologically, it is likely that digital art will continue to push the boundaries of mainstream culture and provoke new forms of artistic expression and interpretation.
User: Can you provide some examples of digital art that have gained mainstream recognition and helped to increase awareness of the possibilities of digital technology in the art world?
Assistant: Yes, certainly. There have been several examples of digital art gaining mainstream recognition, helping to increase awareness of the potential of digital technology in the art world. Here are a few prominent examples:

1. The work of Yayoi Kusama: Kusama's immersive installations, which feature patterns of dots and bright colors, have gained significant attention in recent years. Her famous Infinity Mirror Rooms installations incorporate mirrors, lights, and polka dots to create a kaleidoscopic effect. These installations are excellent examples of how digital technology can be used to create interactive, immersive art experiences. 2. The use of digital projection mapping: Projection mapping has been used in several public installations, including the 2012 London Olympics’ opening ceremony. The technology consists of using light and images to transform the appearance of a building's facade or entire urban spaces like streets and parks, creating an interactive and immersive experience for viewers. 3. Ai Weiwei's installation art: The acclaimed artist and human rights advocate, Ai Weiwei, is highly regarded for his digital installations exploring themes like censorship and human rights. His work often includes digital media, such as video projections, photographs, and social media tools, to speak directly to his audience and engage them with his message. 4. Jason Salavon's data-based art: Jason Salavon's work involves creating art based on large data sets. For example, he creates highly detailed pixelated artworks of landscapes by compiling thousands of images of the same scene found online. Salavon's work serves as an example of how digital technology can be used to make sense of vast amounts of data and create unique and complex artworks. In conclusion, these examples illustrate how digital technology can be used to create a wide range of art forms, from immersive installations to data-driven artworks. By exploring new technologies, artists can challenge traditional notions of what is considered "art" and create new and innovative art forms, bringing digital technology to the forefront of contemporary art.

Assistant: Janelle had always felt like she was lost, wandering through life without any real direction or purpose. As a child, she had tried her hand at various hobbies and sports, but nothing had ever really clicked for her. That all changed one day when she stumbled upon an art class by chance.

The class was being held in a little community center, and Janelle had only gone in because it was raining outside and she had nothing better to do. She watched as the instructor demonstrated different techniques with charcoal and paint, and something within her stirred. She knew immediately that this was what she had been missing.

Over the next few years, Janelle poured herself into her newfound passion. She started with simple sketches, but soon moved on to more complex pieces. She didn't have any formal training, but she was a natural – her art was full of life and emotion, and people couldn't help but be drawn to it.

Despite this, Janelle still struggled with self-doubt. She didn't believe that she had what it took to make it as an artist, and even though people were always praising her work, she felt like she was just fumbling around in the dark.

That all changed when she met Adele. Adele was an older woman, with white hair and a sharp wit. They met by chance at an art supply store, and Adele struck up a conversation with Janelle about a particular shade of blue that she was considering. They soon became fast friends.

Adele was an accomplished artist, with years of experience and a studio full of paintings that took Janelle's breath away. At first, Janelle was intimidated by her, but Adele was patient with her and took her under her wing.

As they worked together, Janelle began to realize that her self-doubt was keeping her from fully embracing her talent. She was so worried about what other people thought of her work that she couldn't see how truly gifted she was.

One day, Adele took Janelle to an art show that she was participating in. As they walked around, Janelle was struck by the beauty and variety of the other artists' works. It was intimidating, but it also inspired her.

Adele's paintings were stunning, and Janelle could see how much time and effort had gone into them. Impulsively, she turned to her friend and said, "I want to do this too. I want to be an artist."

Adele's smile was warm and kind. "You already are, my dear," she said. "You just need to believe it for yourself."

Over the next few months, Janelle worked harder than she ever had before. She poured all of her emotions into her art, and the results were breathtaking. She submitted some of her work to a local gallery, and to her surprise, they accepted it.

The night of the opening was like nothing Janelle had ever experienced. There were so many people, all admiring her art and congratulating her on her talent. She felt like she was on top of the world.

But even in that moment of triumph, Janelle knew that she still had work to do. She couldn't let her self-doubt control her anymore. She had to trust in herself and her talent, even when things were difficult.

It wasn't always easy, but Janelle persevered. She continued to create art that touched people's hearts and inspired them. She learned to love her own work, flaws and all.

In the end, Janelle realized that her true talent was not just in her art, but in her ability to push past her fears and doubts. She had found her passion in art, but it was her inner strength that allowed her to truly shine.
User: Hey, that short story is really great! Can you add more details about how Janelle's artwork evolved over the years? I'd like to know more about how she developed her talent.
Assistant: Certainly! As Janelle pursued her passion for art, she began to experiment with different mediums and techniques. At first, she stuck to basic sketching with charcoal and graphite. She started out by drawing simple still lifes, like vases of flowers or bowls of fruit, but soon began to add her own creative touches to these pieces.

As Janelle became more comfortable with the basics, she started to branch out. She worked with watercolors and acrylics, exploring how colors and textures could convey different moods and emotions. She honed her skills in portraiture, creating detailed and lifelike images of people she knew.

But even as Janelle's technical abilities improved, she still struggled with self-doubt. She would often compare her own work to that of other artists, and wonder if she would ever be as good as they were. It was only after she met Adele that she began to understand that true talent wasn't just about being technically skilled, but about the emotion and meaning that one could bring to their work.

With Adele's guidance, Janelle learned to let go of her self-doubt and create from the heart. She started to incorporate more abstract elements into her pieces, allowing her emotions to guide her brushstrokes. She also began to experiment with mixed media, creating collages that combined photographs, cutouts, and paint.

In the end, Janelle's artwork became a reflection of her own journey. Each piece was imbued with her own emotions and experiences, capturing a moment in time in a way that was uniquely hers. Her work became sought after by collectors who were captivated by the raw beauty and emotion conveyed in her art.

Looking back on her journey, Janelle realized that it wasn't just about finding her talent, but about growing and evolving as an artist. She had come a long way from the hesitant, self-doubting girl she once was, and she was excited to see where her talent would take her next.
User: This short story is amazing! Can you add more details about Janelle's relationship with Adele? I'd love to know more about how they met and how their friendship developed over time.

Feeling brave, Janelle struck up a conversation with Adele, asking her about the colors she was considering. Adele was friendly and warm from the start, and the two began chatting about art and life in general. It was clear that they shared a similar passion for creating, and the conversation felt effortless.

Before long, Adele suggested that they go for a coffee together, and Janelle eagerly agreed. They spent hours talking over coffee, sharing stories about their lives and discussing different techniques they had used in their art. From that point on, they started to see each other regularly, always finding new ways to inspire and support each other.

Over time, Adele became like a second mother to Janelle. She encouraged her to dig deeper in her artwork, to push past her insecurities, and to embrace her own creativity. Adele had years of experience to share, and Janelle soaked up every piece of advice she could get.

Their friendship was a true meeting of minds, and there was an ease and comfort to their conversations that Janelle had never experienced with anyone else. Adele had a way of seeing the best in Janelle, and she always provided a safe and nurturing space for her to explore her artistry.

As their friendship deepened, Janelle realized that Adele's influence had not only helped her art to blossom but had also brought so much richness into her life. She was grateful for the chance encounter that had brought them together, and for the way that Adele's friendship had changed the course of her life.
User: This short story is fantastic! I really enjoyed reading about Janelle's journey and how she discovered her true talent. Can you add more details about how Janelle's art affected people who saw it? I'd like to know more about their reactions and how it made Janelle feel.

They marveled at the way that Janelle was able to capture human emotion so vividly, and they were moved by the passion that she infused into every brushstroke.

As Janelle progressed in her artistic journey, her work continued to captivate viewers. One of her earliest admirers was a woman who saw one of Janelle's charcoal sketches in a coffee shop. The woman was visibly moved by the piece, and she approached Janelle to ask if she could buy it. Janelle was shocked and thrilled – she had never thought that her work would be good enough to sell.

Over time, Janelle began to participate in art shows and gallery exhibits. People from all over came to see her work and to meet the talented artist behind it. And it wasn't just art enthusiasts who were impressed - even casual observers were struck by the beauty and emotional depth of Janelle's creations.

Janelle didn't just receive praise when her art was displayed in public, however. She also touched the lives of those closest to her. Her friends and family members were awed by the way that she was able to capture their essence in her paintings and drawings. Some even said that seeing Janelle's work helped them to understand themselves or their own emotions in a new way.

Perhaps the most moving response Janelle ever received from her art, however, came from a complete stranger. One day, while setting up for an exhibit at a local gallery, a woman approached Janelle and started to cry. She explained that she had just gone through a difficult personal struggle and that Janelle's artwork had helped her to process her emotions and find hope again. The woman told Janelle that her paintings had saved her life.

It was moments like these that made Janelle feel incredibly grateful for her talent. She was humbled and awed by the way that her art was able to touch people in such deep and meaningful ways. For Janelle, it wasn't just about making beautiful pictures - it was about creating a connection with others, and making the world a little brighter in the process.
